caption: The video showcases two concentric ring assemblies resting on a plain white surface, each built from alternating flat circular disc faces and upright ring-shaped spacers. At the top edge a human hand is already in place, its fingers pinching one upright washer on the upper arc of the outer ring and holding it steady while the rest of the structure remains undisturbed. The flat discs on the upper-left portion of the outer ring carry a warm reddish tint, a reflection cast by the nearby skin. As time passes, the fingers loosen their grip and the hand drifts upward, moving out of sight entirely and leaving the assemblies untouched. With the hand gone, that reddish reflection fades from the disc faces, which settle into a neutral silver tone matching the rest of the metalwork. The inner ring and the remaining outer components stay fixed in their positions, without visible rotation or translation. The viewpoint stays steady, so the only visible motion is the withdrawal of the hand and the gradual clearing of its reflection. The two ring structures continue to lie flat and still on the white background.
